page.layout: One page of text in a single column; marginal notes in the left margin (references and short notes) and right margin (catchword-style notes); running head at top; signature at foot.

main_text.p: suspendito. De Cruce accipi res docet, & Cicero, qui in eâ pro Rabirio palàm sic interpretatur. & Epist. cx.Seneca: Inuenitur qui velit adactus ad infelix illud Infelix lignum.lignum trahere animam tot tormenta tracturam.
In Octa-uio.Minutius Felix: Deus ligneus, rogi fortasse vel infelicis stipitis portio: id est, crucis. Dixit & Infamem Infelix stipes. Infamis stipes.In Catal. Virg.Poëta incertus

p.i: Noxius infami districtus stipite membra, Sperat & à fixâ posse redire Cruce.

main_text.p: Natæ appellationes à judicio & sensu vulgi, quibus hoc supplicium in horrore pariter & vilitate. Itaque Apuleius (in meo quidem & prisco libro) Lib. 1. de Asin.Damnatam Crucem dixit. *Damnata, inquit, jam Crucis candidatus: bene, & pro hoc sensu. Etsi autem Crux proprie in ligno: tamen adnoto, similitudine etiam itâ dictam suspensionem aut fixionem in aliâ paratura, puta in monte aut petrâ. Sic Lib. 1. ad-uersus Marc. cap. 1.Tertulliano sunt Cruces Caucasorum, alludenti ad Promethea illic affixum: quem ipsum Lucianus describit & appellat σαυρωθέντα. Sic & Manilius de Andromedâ, quæ in scopulo vincta & ceto exposita: Lib. v.Et cruce virgine à moritura puella pependit.
main_text.head: CAP. III.
Nomina phrasesque ad hoc supplicium: Figere, Configere, Cruciare. item Cruciarius, pro appendendo.
main_text.p: CRVCIS hæc nomina: supplicij quod per eam, ista. Cruci suffigere. vt Velleius de piratis, quos Cæsar, inquit, Cruci suffixit. In cruce suf-figere.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the left and right are partly faint and abbreviated; the right-margin note "Cruces in petrâ" and the asterisked "*Vulgo destinata" are placed beside their lines. The first and final words on lines are reconstructed from the scan where the print is faint. Catchword absent; page ends with "figere".
